body:
15 Nov 2026, THE ADVISOR'S RULINGS on the three decisions of the N-34 design (PR #96), and the lead's read-only check.
1. THE PAIR stays HELD (the default). Check on VM 108, 15 Nov ~13:30 UTC: the two Creature refs (sr_...S0ACZ7 '[Unknown Album]', sr_...EWEMF7 the real album) are in DIFFERENT playlists (3 playlists hold the first, 4 the second, NO playlist holds both); no play history, no saved album refs; the entries come from imports (3 and 8 import entries). So merging them by identity later (slice 6) would not put one song twice in a playlist; it is still not done in the repair's first run: the repair already carries an unproven risk (does Navidrome keep a song's id across a move) and the 14 Nov ruling on the five held pairs applies by precedent: one irreversible step at a time, no file deletion in the same run.
2. THE ONE-TIME RE-DOWNLOAD of a repaired downloaded song is ACCEPTED, on Wi-Fi. refAudioKey hashes the file size (fingerprint.dart:101), so EVERY later repair that rewrites tags (N-26 slice 5 shares the machinery, and any future retag) triggers another re-download: a cost to the future (rule 1). Filed as the audio-only key item (number assigned at merge: N-38: N-36 and N-37 are helper-p225 items in PR #98). TRIGGER: built BEFORE any second tag-rewriting repair ships (N-26 slice 5). Not built now.
3. A SINGLE becomes its own release (title as album, track 1, its own folder), as Spotify does and as the 'Singles and EPs' shelf already shows ('Creature, 2024 - Single'). RIDER: placement._existing_child reuses any folder of the same name ignoring case and punctuation, so a single that shares its title with an existing ALBUM folder of that artist (a title track released first) would land inside the album's folder: the design must say how the two are told apart (add a test row to the slice that places files: a single 'Hollow' and an album 'Hollow' of one artist).
OVERRULES ACCEPTED: P2-25 moved before N-34 (the needs forces it; the owner said yes to moving P2-25 up on 7 Nov); RELEASE-CANDIDATE 4b gate for slices 1-3 (no stranger makes a bucket). COSTS ON THE BOARD: every item added to 4b pushes b11 back, and b11 is what unlocks P2-12 (which N-33 'play all' needs): if the owner says YES to lifting D-51, revisit the order. B-133: confirm no other PR took the number before #96 merges.
